big_case.notes: Routine last-minute capital stay application arising from a successive state postconviction denial; presents a recurring, repeatedly rejected Woodard clemency challenge with no circuit split, no amicus participation, no response call from the Court, and a summary unsigned denial without noted dissent.

leakage.notes: Forward prediction placed on 2026-11-04T01:40:43Z, one day before the November 5, 2026 disposition. Retrieval log records only local file reads of the staged arrival record and one corpus query for companion cert petition 26-6013.

central_claims.basis: On November 5, 2026, the docket entry reads verbatim: 'Application (26A623) for a stay of execution of sentence of death, submitted to Justice Thomas, and by him referred to the Court, is denied.'
central_claims.claim: Justice Thomas will refer Application 26A623 to the full Court, and the Court will deny the stay application in a one-sentence unsigned order on or before November 5, 2026.

central_claims.basis: outcome.json records interim_signals.response_requested = false and amicus_briefs = 0; snapshot 2026-11-05.json shows Florida filed its response on November 2 and Guardado replied on November 3 without a Court order requesting a response.
central_claims.claim: The State of Florida will file an opposition brief on its own initiative under capital practice without the Court entering a formal response-requested order (response_requested: false).

central_claims.basis: outcome.json records votes: [], noted_dissent_from_denial: null, and writing_roles: null; no Justice wrote separately or noted a dissent on the November 5, 2026 order.
central_claims.claim: No Justice will write a separate opinion or publicly note a dissent from the denial.

central_claims.basis: The Court denied the application in a single-sentence unsigned order without stating a doctrinal rationale.
central_claims.claim: The application fails the Nken / Hill v. McDonough stay standard because there is no reasonable probability of four votes for certiorari in 26-6013 on a Woodard clemency claim asserting no split of authority and relying only on post-1983 Florida clemency statistics and gubernatorial statements.
